packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-05 - unverified image reading (first reader)

EXPOSURE / PROCEDURE NOTE
No proposed identification or earlier reading of this item was in my context. (Before this
packet I read packet-04, a Greek item, as instructed; nothing there bears on this one.)
I listed the packet directory once for file names; packet.json was not opened.

LAYOUT SURVEY, FACE 1 (image-001.jpg, reduced overview)
Observations:
- Colour photograph taken at a steep oblique angle into the gutter of a bound book. A
  narrow parchment strip (binding waste: a guard or spine lining) runs vertically; a sewing
  support with thread is visible at the top right, loose threads at the bottom.
- The strip carries Latin text in a small Gothic book hand (textualis), brown ink, heavily
  abbreviated. Only the right-hand part of each line is visible; line beginnings lie to
  the left where the strip is faded/abraded and out of focus, and line ends disappear into
  the gutter at the right. About 12 lines visible.
- No rubric, running title, initial, underlining or gloss visible. Whether the parent leaf
  had one or two columns cannot be told from this crop.
- Orientation: text upright relative to the book, slightly rotated by the camera angle.
Tiles image-002.jpg (upper half) and image-003.jpg (lower half) overlap by about two lines.

FACE 1 TRANSCRIPTION (line beginnings lost/blurred at left, line ends in gutter at right;
"[...]" at either end = text continues out of view)

image-002.jpg (upper half)
 1: [...] c[..]uꝫ(?) [...]                      (top line, only tops/abraded traces)
 2: [...] aa[..]e(?) [illegible] [...]
 3: [...] sangui(n)e(?) [illegible] aīa(?) [...]   ("aīa"/"aiu" with stroke above, at the gutter)
 4: [...] nō d[..]t(?) [illegible] t(ibi?) c(?)/ tc̄(?) [...]
 5: [...] mīo[..]ſ[..] [.]ibu(s?) [...]            (first group with a stroke above: "mīo.."/"m(inist)..."?)
 6: [...] [..]am[..] [..]uni [...]                 (faint; perhaps "...am ... uni/um")
 7: [...] c(um?)/ex(?) p[.]o [..]t[..] [...]       (out of focus; continues in image-003 line 1)
 8: [...] [m]o[...] c(om)mūn[...]                  (only lower edge of tile; = image-003 line 2)

image-003.jpg (lower half; lines 1-2 repeat image-002 lines 7-8)
 1: [...] [..]p po[..] [..]ini(?) [...]
 2: [...] [illegible] c(om)mūn(..) [...]           (clear: "c̄mūn" with abbreviation stroke)
 3: [...] mo[..]ꝫ q̄ ē cꝫ(?) [...]                   (reading "mo[rt]ꝫ(?) q(ue) e(st) c..ꝫ" - uncertain;
                                                    the group at the gutter is "ēcꝫ" or "ēeꝫ" with a mark below)
 4: [...] p(er?) aīa(m?) tuā(m?) · p(er) mi(..) [...]   ("aiā" and "tuā" blurred; "pmi" clear, p with crossed tail)
 5: [...] saluꝫ(?) fac(er)e(?) [..]bꝫ aliu(d?) [...]     ("...bꝫ aliu" at the gutter is clear)
 6: [...] a(?) · po[r]tār[.] [.] si aliqu(..) [...]      (first word with stroke above: "pōtār"/"portār"; end
                                                         "aliqu" partly behind thread)
 [loose sewing threads cross the last line]

Remarks on face 1: none of these lines gives a complete clause; the visible strip is perhaps
a third of a line wide. The clearest strings for matching are "c̄mūn", "p mi", "bꝫ aliu",
"si aliqu", and (less sure) "sangui...", "p aīa tuā", "saluꝫ fac".

----------------------------------------------------------------------
LAYOUT SURVEY, SECOND VIEW (image-004.jpg, reduced overview)
Observations:
- Frontal colour photograph, with ruler (cm) and colour target, of a paper leaf in the same
  or a similar binding; the leaf is the right-hand page, with the gutter at the left.
- On the paper leaf (not the object of the strips): at upper right a block of faint pen
  notes in a later cursive, about five short lines, one group underlined and reading like a
  number, "1522"(?) / "1322"(?) - too small to read here; show-through of large printed
  or display lettering in the middle of the leaf (reversed, from the other side); a faint
  ink note lower centre ending "... possidet."; a purple shelf stamp at lower right:
  "SCAFFALE 58 [..]" / "PALCHETTO C [.]" and beside it "8" and a cancelled stamp.
- In the gutter at the left, two parchment strips with Gothic script, one above and one
  below a sewing station:
    upper strip - about ten short line-fragments, WRITTEN UPSIDE DOWN relative to the book
                  (a capital touched with red at its lower end);
    lower strip - about six short line-fragments, upright.
  Only 2-5 letters of each line are exposed.
Tiles: image-005.jpg = upper strip; image-006.jpg = lower strip (its top repeats the last
line of image-005).

image-005.jpg - upper strip. The writing is inverted in the image. To read it I made a
180-degree rotated working copy of the tile (disclosed as a step beyond simply viewing).
Line numbers are counted from the top of the image AS SUPPLIED; the text therefore runs
from line 10 upward to line 1. Each fragment is the BEGINNING of a line (left margin of the
original text is the visible edge after rotation); the rest of each line is under the
paste-down/gutter.
 10: Se[.] [...]      (capital S with a red vertical stroke; then "e" and a cut letter - "Sec"/"Seq"/"Sed"?)
  9: fio'(?) [...]    ("fi" + o with a superscript sign: "fio(n)"/"fid'"?)
  8: quo [...]        (a small mark above before it)
  7: mis [...]        (or "ims"; i-stroke visible; long s at the cut)
  6: fidel [...]      ("fidel" - last letter cut, l or tall stroke)
  5: bōiu(?) [...]    (b, o with stroke above, then minims: "bōn.."/"bōiu..")
  4: ꝛc̄t(?) / 2ctr(?) [...]   (begins with a 2-shaped sign (et/r-rotunda) then "ct"/"cc" and a cut letter)
  3: th'(?) [...]     ("t" + "h" with a hook: "th(?)" / "tħ")
  2: hu[..] [...]     (abraded; stroke above)
  1: [.]u[..] [...]   (traces under paper debris)

image-006.jpg - lower strip, upright. Here the fragments are line ENDS (right edge of a
text block), the beginnings being under the gutter fold at the left.
 1: (repeat of image-005 line 10: red-stroked S, seen inverted)
 2: [sewing station, no text]
 3: [...] ora.        (with a rising stroke above: "ōra."/"-o(r)ra."; punctus after)
 4: [...] o tp̄s       ("tp̄s" with abbreviation stroke = t(em)p(u)s; preceded by "o" or "d")
 5: [...] tec.        (or "cec."/"ecc."; a small sign above; punctus after)
 6: [...] lias        (or "tias"/"cias"; final long s)
 7: [...] itaꝫ(?)     ("ita" + a final abbreviation sign, -tas/-tatꝫ?)
 8: [...] [..]ato(?)  (abraded; a wavy mark above)

----------------------------------------------------------------------
LAYOUT SURVEY, THIRD VIEW (image-007.jpg, reduced overview; image-009.jpg is the same
opening photographed again, turned 90 degrees with the gutter at the bottom)
Observations:
- Frontal colour photograph with ruler and colour target: a blank paper leaf/pastedown on
  the left, the gutter at the right. Along the gutter four separate parchment pieces are
  pasted, separated by the sewing stations (ruler positions approx.):
    strip I   (c. 0.5-6.5 cm): Gothic script, c. 10 line-fragments, with a red rubric or
               red heading fragment at its top edge; the writing is UPSIDE DOWN relative
               to the book. Tile: image-008.jpg.
    strip II  (c. 7-14 cm): almost blank parchment; one isolated red sign in the middle,
               looking like two paragraph marks or "66." in red (image-007; in image-009
               it appears as a red sign too). No other text seen.
    strip III (c. 15-21.5 cm): a piece pasted with its text running ALONG the spine (lines
               parallel to the gutter), three lines, rust-stained. Tile: image-010.jpg.
    strip IV  (c. 23-28.5 cm): Gothic script, upright, c. 10-12 line-fragments - by its
               line pattern ("nō d..", "mi..", "mo..", "p aiā", "salu..") this is the
               same piece as FACE 1 (image-001 to -003), here seen frontally and small.
               No separate tile of it in this view.
- In image-009 a further piece with script is visible at the far end of the gutter (left
  in that image, c. 27-31 cm on its ruler), lines again running across the strip; this
  looks like strip IV seen from the other direction, but the overview is too small to be sure.
- No running titles, initials or glosses visible on any strip. Red is present on strip I
  (rubric) and strip II (sign), and one red-stroked capital on the upper strip of the
  second view.
Tentative interpretation: all strips are cut from one or more leaves of the same Gothic
manuscript and reused as spine linings/guards; I cannot show from these images that they
come from a single leaf.

image-008.jpg - strip I. The writing is inverted in the image; read from a 180-degree
rotated working copy (same disclosure as above). Line numbers count from the top of the
image AS SUPPLIED, so the text runs from line 11 upward. The fragments are line ENDS
(right-hand edge of a text block; a wide blank margin follows).
 11: [...] [.]ē(?)        (one or two letters with a stroke above, damaged)
 10: [...] [..]mū         (minims + u with stroke: "-mū"/"-inū")
  9: [...] [..]nui(?)     (minims: "-nui"/"-mu"/"-iuu")
  8: [...] [..]tiō / ciō  (clear "o" with a stroke above; hole/dark spot above the line)
  7: [...] [..]no cc̄(?)   ("no" then two c-shaped letters with a wavy stroke above: "cc̄"/"ec̄"/"tc̄")
  6: [...] [..]ā(?)       (damaged letters + "a" with a long stroke above; a small flourish after)
  5: [...] [.]t dō(?)     (possibly "-t do"/"-rdo"; damaged)
  4: [...] bn̄ / br̄(?)     ("b" + a letter with stroke above; a small cross-like mark above the line)
  3: [...] q̄ ha(?) .      ("q" then "ha"/"ba", punctus after)
  2: [...] [..]mū(?)      (damaged; minims + stroke)
  1: [red] [..]L[..]ic(?) [...]   (rubric fragment in red, abraded; in the supplied orientation it
                                  appears at the top as two red groups; I cannot read it securely)

image-010.jpg - strip III, three lines, upright in this tile (in the book they run along
the spine). The left half of the strip is blank parchment (margin), so these are line
BEGINNINGS, cut at the right by the strip edge. Much rust spotting; line 3 is cut through
horizontally by the lower edge/fold.
 1: d[..]an[..]t(?) [illegible] ⁊ uen[..]e rc(?) [...]
       (starts with a round d/ꝺ; middle hidden by a rust patch; then the Tironian et "⁊" and
        a word in minims ending "...e"; last visible letters "rc"/"re")
 2: tēp(or)e(?)/tēp(or)is(?) plus(?) penitēcie(?) o[...]
       ("tēp" with stroke is fairly clear; second word begins with p and has long s;
        third word "peni" + "tēcie/tēcia", then "o" at the cut)
 3: debiles(?)/de bl[..](?) [illegible] [...]    (upper halves of letters only)

----------------------------------------------------------------------
SELECTED / UNREAD
- Read: every exposed line-fragment on face 1 (strip IV) and on the upper/lower gutter
  strips of the second view, strip I and strip III. All are partial lines; no span of
  connected prose of ten full lines exists on what is exposed.
- Not read: the later pen notes and the shelf stamp details on the paper leaf in image-004
  (only what is given above); strip II (blank except the red sign); the far-left piece in
  image-009.
- I cannot tell from the images whether the two gutter strips of the second view
  (image-005/-006) are the reverse sides of strips I-IV or different pieces.

SUGGESTIONS
- A frontal, in-focus tile of strip IV (face 1) - the supplied tiles of it are oblique and
  soft at the left.
- A tile of the far-left piece in image-009, and a raking/UV image of strip III line 1.
- If the strips can be lifted or imaged from the fold, the hidden parts of the lines would
  turn these fragments into matchable text.

LIMITATIONS
- Only 2-12 letters per line are exposed; line beginnings or ends are under paste or in
  the gutter. Word division is often a guess.
- Two tiles show inverted script; I rotated working copies of the supplied tiles by 180
  degrees to read them. That is the only thing I did beyond viewing PROMPT.md and the
  packet images (apart from the directory listing noted at the top).
- Abbreviation expansions in parentheses are proposals; "?" marks readings I would not
  rely on; "/" separates open alternatives.
- This is an unverified image reading.
